topics.topic: Representation and revision/access-version binding of pending confirmations for revisionless actions, including import and audit-log erasure
questions: Can an OwnerSession pending confirmation explicitly carry no revision/access version, and if so is that absence a modeled fact distinct from a missing binding?
What revision/access-version binding does the confirmation for audit-log erasure carry?
What revision/access-version binding does an import confirmation carry?
How is a confirmation with no revision or access version represented in the OwnerSession model: is that fact absent, a distinct sentinel value, or is such a confirmation impossible?
What occupies the revision-or-access-version binding for import and audit-entry erasure confirmations?
How is the revision/access-version component of a pending confirmation represented and digested when the target has no revision?
May the audit-erasure confirmation omit the revision/access-version component, and if so what exactly is bound in its place?
What occupies the revision/access-version component of an import confirmation, and does A13's no-revision exception cover an action that creates records rather than acting on a revisionless record?

quotes:
Facts: its identity, minted by Registry at sign-in ("Identity formats");
written once: the instant it began, its expiry at the latest and its CSRF
value (R0-29); changed by the owner's requests (State 2 A13, A16; owner,
2026-10-31): the instant of its last request, which starts as the instant it
began; at most one pending confirmation — its one-time value, the action, its
target, the revision or access version and the inputs it is bound to, and
the instant it was shown — made when a confirmation step is shown, replaced
by the next one shown and cleared when used; and at most one uploaded import
file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted.

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed — or that it showed none, for a record without a
   revision (A04 rule 3) — and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.

An anonymised project and an
   erased Customer have no revision (M01, M04): an action on them states
   none.

An erasure that removes no entry still writes its own entry naming the
   date, with its confirmation id: R0-66 makes the erasure leave an entry of
   its own, whatever it removed.

The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
   step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.
judgement.divergence: One implementer represents and digests an explicit no-version binding for every confirmed action lacking a revision or access version, allowing repeated anonymisation, import and audit-log erasure; another permits no-version only for an existing revisionless Project or Customer, making import and audit-log erasure impossible to confirm, which the owner notices.
judgement.why: The texts permit an explicit no-revision binding only for a record without a revision but require confirmations for import and audit-log erasure, which have no such target, without defining what their version binding contains.

witness.initial: The audit log contains entries older than 2026-10-01, and the owner has a valid owner session.
events: The owner asks Registry to erase audit entries before 2026-10-01.
Registry attempts to show the required confirmation step.
The owner submits the displayed confirmation with the same cutoff date.
outcomes: Registry binds the confirmation to an explicit no-version value, removes the eligible entries and appends the erasure entry.
Registry cannot create or validate the confirmation because the action has neither a revision/access version nor a record without a revision, so the erasure is refused or cannot be submitted.
basis:
The audit log's period is the governance's. In the periodic review the owner
erases, confirming, every entry older than a date the owner gives; that erasure
leaves an entry of its own naming the date.

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed — or that it showed none, for a record without a
   revision (A04 rule 3) — and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.

topics.topic: Whether A21 was reopened or the security review was repeated and reaffirmed after A04 and A13 changed
questions: After the changes to A04 and A13, is A21 reopened, or has the amended behavior been reviewed and the listed outcomes reaffirmed?
Is A21 now reopened pending a new security review, or were the A04 and A13 changes reviewed and A21 reaccepted?
Is A21 currently reopened, or was the security review re-performed for the changed A04 and A13 rules; if it was re-performed, what are its resulting category outcomes and references?

judgement.why: P1 already decides that changing a decision named by A21 reopens the security review, and the additional A13 change is governed by the same unchanged reopening rule.

precedent.topic: Whether A21 was reopened or the security review repeated after the A04 amendment
quotes: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
precedent.why: Because A04 changed and the concurrency category names A04, A21 is reopened; the unchanged PERFORMED label records the earlier performance but does not override the reopening rule.

topics.topic: Whether A05's repeated-transition invariant is conditional on passing A04 revision checks
questions: Does A05's formal invariant apply only after all A04 checks pass, or does it require every repeated transition to be accepted even when it states the former revision?
Is A05's formal invariant conditional on passing A04's revision check, including the new no-revision rule?

judgement.why: P2 already decides that A05 applies only after every A04 check passes, including the amended stale-revision check for a record that no longer has a revision.

precedent.topic: Whether A05's repeated-transition invariant applies only after A04 revision validation
quotes:
A transition to the state a record is already in, that passes every check
   of A04 rule 6, is accepted and changes nothing: archiving an archived project (R0-12), anonymising an anonymised
   one (R0-71), erasing an erased Customer (Primary actions), restricting a
   restricted Customer, lifting an unrestricted one, ending an ended
   relationship, resuming one that is not ended (R0-84), granting a project
   already in a session's set, making the active project active again,
   clearing an active project that is already clear, registering a registered
   session (R0-53).
precedent.why: A05 expressly conditions its repeated-transition rule on passing every A04 check, so a supplied former revision fails the revision check first.
